title: YAML and Helm join the LanguageSpec registry with conservative reference semantics
context: YAML and Helm were the next demand-backed graph gap after Python and Go. Oliver Sampson's PRs #35, #36, and #41 supplied the implementation, but they were developed from an older fork baseline and therefore had to be reconciled with the current Go registry entry, schema generation 3, HLG resource relationships, and the fail-closed repository scan. The useful semantic target is not to pretend YAML aliases or Helm helpers are function calls; it is to preserve their actual reference relationships without weakening correctness for ordinary YAML or inventing cross-chart bindings.
decision: Add YAML through the existing LanguageSpec registry and model anchors as variable symbols, aliases as references edges, and each document as a fallback file symbol. Tolerate syntax errors only when a YAML source contains Helm/Jinja template markers, excluding GitHub Actions ${{ }} expressions; treat .tpl as inherently templated. Under the nearest ancestor Chart.yaml only, run a deterministic text sidecar that extracts Helm define symbols and include/template references, then widen resolution to YAML siblings in that same chart. Keep ambiguous, cross-chart, and non-chart matches unresolved. Key call attribution by the symbol's array index rather than startByte so overlapping synthetic YAML and Helm symbols remain distinct. Keep the native parser family on tree-sitter 0.21.1: YAML 0.6.x declares that peer, and tree-sitter-python is pinned exactly to 0.23.4 because later 0.23 minors moved to tree-sitter 0.22. This expands indexing and conformance evidence only; Constitution mutation/evaluator scope remains separately proven and TypeScript-scoped.
consequences: YAML anchors and aliases contribute truthful fan-in, fan-out, blast-radius, and component evidence without being mislabeled as calls.
Templated Helm/Jinja YAML no longer makes a complete repository scan fail closed merely because the pre-render source is not valid YAML, while genuinely invalid non-templated YAML still fails closed.
Helm define/include/template edges are scoped to the nearest chart and do not guess across sibling charts or into same-named symbols from another language.

The Helm scanner is deliberately a bounded token scan rather than a full Go-template parser; comment-shaped directives and quoted delimiters remain documented limitations, and nested subchart release-global namespace behavior remains conservative by omission.
The symbol-index attribution contract applies to every language and every consumer of attributeCalls; production consumers and TypeScript, Python, Go, YAML, and Helm regression tests move together.
Dependency currency is bounded by the shared native ABI, not npm's latest tag: moving any grammar to the 0.22/0.25 peer family requires a coordinated runtime-and-platform-matrix migration.
alternatives_rejected: Treat every templated YAML file as clean regardless of content: this would hide genuine syntax failures and would misclassify GitHub Actions ${{ }} expressions as Helm/Jinja templates.
Resolve Helm helper names repository-wide: duplicate helper names in separate charts and unrelated code symbols would fabricate graph edges.
Parse Helm only through tree-sitter-yaml: the YAML grammar loses Go-template action semantics during error recovery, so define/include/template cannot be extracted truthfully from that tree alone.
Use symbol startByte as the caller identity: a synthetic whole-file YAML symbol and a Helm define can both begin at byte zero, collapsing distinct callers.
Broaden Constitution evaluators at the same time: registry breadth is structural indexing breadth, not proof that language-specific mutation or behavior evaluation is sound.
